title: Acid Rain and Our Monuments
summary: How burning fuels turns rain acidic, what it does to marble, forests and lakes, and how India protects the Taj Mahal.

ib.note: Extension: Criterion D, the impacts of science and technology

cbse.chapter: Curiosity Ch 13: Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet (air pollution and acid rain)
Earlier NCERT Class 8 Ch 18: Pollution of Air and Water (acid rain, the Taj Mahal)
Ch 2: Acids, Bases and Salts (rain below pH 5.6 is acid rain)

objectives: I can explain how acid rain forms from sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides.
I can describe the effects of acid rain on buildings, lakes and forests.
I can evaluate solutions to reduce acid rain, including those used to protect the Taj Mahal.
misconceptions: All rain is neutral (clean rain is naturally slightly acidic, about pH 5.6).
Acid rain burns your skin like strong acid.
Acid rain only affects the place where the pollution is made.
